metadata.disclaimer: General guidance only. Recycling rules are set locally and change often. Always confirm with your municipal authority or local facility. This is not a determination of material composition, contamination, or recyclability.

categories.description: Paper and paperboard products such as boxes, office paper and printed materials.
categories.reuse_guidance: Reuse boxes for storage or shipping. Use blank sides of paper for notes or drafts.
categories.disposal_guidance: Keep clean and dry, flatten boxes, and place in paper recycling where accepted. Remove excessive tape and non-paper inserts.
categories.safety_notes: Avoid recycling paper contaminated with food, oil, or chemicals.
categories.contamination_notes: Grease, food residue and moisture lower fibre quality and can cause rejection.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Generally recyclable when clean and dry; laminated, waxed or heavily soiled paper often is not.

categories.description: Plastic bottles, containers and film. Many resin types exist (PET, HDPE, PP, etc.).
categories.reuse_guidance: Refill and reuse containers where safe. Reuse sturdy bags multiple times; keep them out of waterways.
categories.disposal_guidance: Empty and rinse containers. Check the resin code and local acceptance. Film and bags often need a separate drop-off.
categories.safety_notes: Do not reuse containers that held hazardous substances for food. Never burn plastics.
categories.contamination_notes: Food residue and mixed materials (caps, labels, pumps) can reduce recyclability.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Acceptance varies by resin code and facility; only some types are accepted locally.

categories.description: Glass bottles and jars used for food and beverages.
categories.reuse_guidance: Reuse jars for storage. Glass can be recycled many times if it reaches a facility cleanly.
categories.disposal_guidance: Rinse and remove lids. Deposit in glass recycling where accepted, sorting by colour if required.
categories.safety_notes: Broken glass is a cut hazard. Wrap sharp pieces before disposal.
categories.contamination_notes: Ceramics, Pyrex and mirrors are different glass types and usually contaminate the glass stream.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Container glass is commonly recyclable; window glass, ceramics and heat-resistant glass usually are not.

categories.description: Aluminium and steel cans, foil and small metal items.
categories.reuse_guidance: Reuse tins for storage or planting. Clean foil can sometimes be reused.
categories.disposal_guidance: Empty and rinse. Metals are widely recycled, but aerosol and pressurised containers need care.
categories.safety_notes: Watch for sharp edges. Do not place pressurised or reactive containers in normal recycling.
categories.contamination_notes: Heavy food residue should be rinsed; mixed-material packaging may need separation.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Aluminium and steel are generally recyclable where collection exists.

categories.description: Clothing, linens and other fabric items.
categories.reuse_guidance: Donate or swap usable clothing. Cut worn textiles into cleaning rags.
categories.disposal_guidance: Use textile banks or charity collection where available. Avoid placing textiles in general waste if a collection exists.
categories.safety_notes: Sanitise items that may carry contamination. Keep textiles dry.
categories.contamination_notes: Wet or mouldy textiles are often not accepted.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Reuse is prioritised; fibre recycling availability varies by region.

categories.description: Consumer electronics and appliances. These may contain batteries, heavy metals and recoverable materials.
categories.reuse_guidance: Repair or donate working devices. Refurbishers can extend device life.
categories.disposal_guidance: Use certified e-waste collection points or retailer take-back schemes. Do not put electronics in general bins.
categories.safety_notes: Some devices contain batteries that can catch fire if damaged. Never shred or puncture. Consider data wiping before disposal.
categories.contamination_notes: Batteries and accessories should be removed and handled separately where possible.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Electronics are recyclable through specialised streams, not curbside bins.

categories.description: Single-use and rechargeable batteries, including lithium-ion cells.
categories.reuse_guidance: Rechargeable batteries can be reused via chargers; avoid mixing chemistries.
categories.disposal_guidance: Take all batteries to a battery or hazardous-waste drop-off. Never place in curbside bins.
categories.safety_notes: Damaged or swollen lithium batteries are a fire risk. Tape terminals and store away from flammables.
categories.contamination_notes: Mixing battery types can short-circuit and cause fires.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Recyclable through specialised battery programs; curbside disposal is not appropriate.

categories.description: Food scraps, garden waste and other compostable material.
categories.reuse_guidance: Compost at home where possible; use for gardens or community compost schemes.
categories.disposal_guidance: Use organics/compost collection if available; otherwise compost or dispose responsibly.
categories.safety_notes: Avoid composting meat, dairy or oils in small home systems; they attract pests.
categories.contamination_notes: Plastic bags, stickers and packaging contaminate compost streams.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Composting depends on local programs and material type.

categories.description: Items with multiple materials or where the model could not make a reliable material claim.
categories.reuse_guidance: Consider whether the item can be reused as-is before disposal.
categories.disposal_guidance: Follow local guidance for the item. Contact your municipality when unsure. Do not assume recyclability.
categories.safety_notes: If the item is unknown and could be hazardous, handle with caution.
categories.contamination_notes: Mixed materials are often difficult to separate and may not be accepted.
categories.recyclability_conditions: Unknown; depends on exact materials and local facilities.
